title: Knowledge check: Handling Files with Multer or Equivalent Middleware

questions.prompt: In Handling Files with Multer or Equivalent Middleware, which statement best describes Single-file uploads?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Treat filenames, MIME types and file contents as untrusted. Limit request size, generate storage names, constrain resolved paths, and keep private objects outside a public static directory.
This option describes a different concept and does not define single-file uploads (choice 2).
questions.answer_key: Treat filenames, MIME types and file contents as untrusted. Limit request size, generate storage names, constrain resolved paths, and keep private objects outside a public static directory.
questions.explanation: Treat filenames, MIME types and file contents as untrusted. Limit request size, generate storage names, constrain resolved paths, and keep private objects outside a public static directory.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Handling Files with Multer or Equivalent Middleware?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.
questions.explanation: Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.

questions.prompt: A change related to Handling Files with Multer or Equivalent Middleware appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
